title: Exact discriminant perfect-power extraction
objective: Accelerate maximal-exponent perfect-power extraction for large discriminant components with one source-transparent arbitrary-integer call, exact host validation, positive and negative semantics, portable fallback, differential oracles, and degree-90 phase evidence
references: Prime-exponent extraction theorem for maximal integer perfect powers

handoff.summary: Rejected performance experiment. The one-call source-transparent extractor preserves maximal-exponent semantics for positive and negative inputs, validates exact identities and primitive returned bases, agrees across CPython/dynamic/compiled paths, rejects corruption, and preserves exact degree-90 components and certificate replay. It is nevertheless slower than the readable bigint implementation. The sole bounded sample measured the perfect-power phase at 1.716365s compiled versus 1.348780s readable (0.785835x), full decomposition at 6.887716s versus 6.624623s (0.961803x), and the representative 15,186-bit call at 562.951ms versus 424.450ms (0.753973x). This backend is rejected and must not be production-selected.
risks: The source-level binary-power and Newton loops duplicate operations already optimized by the host bigint implementation and regress the measured target.
The compiler-compatible source was removed after its exact negative receipt was committed; shipping or selecting it would slow degree-90 decomposition.
next_steps: Retain the benchmark receipt, bound to its historical source commit, as negative evidence.
Investigate a mature GMP/FLINT exact root primitive or reduce repeated classification calls before attempting another perfect-power acceleration.
